- owns: `<sub>/operations/<id>`, `<sub>/opsteps/<id>/<i>`, `<sub>/opdone/<id>/<i>`, `<sub>/opcount/<id>`, `<sub>/opbusy/<root>`, `<sub>/operations-turn`, `<sub>/operations-epoch`;
- reads: `platform/manifest/<sub>`, `domain/keys`, `domain/revoked`, `domain/holder`, `domain/disabled`.
- The operation `<id>` is named by the caller of the door «accept»: the caller's memory row carries the operation id and lands in the same batch, so the caller needs the id before the batch.
- `iat` of the operation row is the input of step 4a of the right contract on the step callbacks: a token older than the assignment `admin` does not serve step 4a.
- The operation doors give out `state` `paused` if not `done` and `paused` or `expired` is set.
The console compares roots only for equality.
The root of an unfinished operation is busy, on pause included. Acceptances without common roots do not contend: the rows differ.
The leader does not re-read a foreign new version as the person's consent: a foreign edit gives the step `fail` and does not pass silently.
The id of the object created by a step is `created_id` of its outcome.\n\nVectors — [`op-step`](../vectors/op-step/README.md).
- `code` of an outcome `ok` or `fail` is the subsystem's code; the console does not parse it.
At finishing an operation, the counters give `done = total`.
The acceptance batch is limited by the weight (the configured `-max-body` of the store, declared by its daemon-flags form, [P/01.3](../../01-store/spec/01.3-store.norms.md)), not by `BATCH_WRITES`.

The occupancy-row weight follows from the key and value forms of N1.2; at most `OPS_STEPS_MAX` distinct roots contribute such rows to the batch. The weight of the memory row is held by the ceiling of the subsystem's table.
The value of the secret of a step is stored open nowhere.
At the operation doors, a longer path — `404 no such path`.
At the operation doors, `<id>` not of 32 lowercase hex — `404 no such operation`.
- at a table without `service`: `view` is there, `edit` is not — `403 denied` at `pause`, `resume`, `cancel`, `retry-failed`;
- at a table without `service`: no `edit` at acceptance — `403 denied`.
With `service: true` the right on the table is not judged:\nacceptance goes by the right of consequences, the person's right is judged on the targets of the steps.

With `service: true` a person sees only their own operation: `by` of the record ≠ `user` of the ticket — `404 no such operation` on reading and control, a foreign operation is as if\nit did not exist.
With `service: true` the translation introduces no rows `sub: <s>` on the table.
Every step callback checks the fresh `may` of the author on every row of the batch.
The console does not read the answer body of the step call.

The transport, headers, the answer type and the network timeouts of the step call are as at the pass of the gate-and-pass contract «Pass of the second kind»: the same path, the same `X-W2C-Pass-Ticket`. The address and the callback listener — there too.
The console gives the worker's answer to the step call to no one.
The deadline of the step call is `OPS_STEP_WAIT`.
The step ticket lives while the step call is open.
There is no exception for the deadline of the step ticket: the deadline has passed — `401`, the operation goes on pause (N3 «step»).

- in a step batch, `writes` carries exactly one row `<sub>/opdone/<id>/<i>` of its own step `cas ""` and the row `<sub>/opcount/<id>` with `cas`. A row of a foreign step or a foreign operation — `403 denied`: the ticket gives a write of only these two rows;
At `412 leader moved` the subsystem ends the step call and does not write the outcome `fail`.

`412 leader moved` is not an outcome of the step, so it does not go into the memory of `step_key`: it arises after the claim, at step 5 of the door's procedure (reconciliation by read) or at step 9 (`412 guard` of the store, [chapter 6.1](06.1-console.norms.md) «batch»), and there the door removes its `pending`; the target is reliably not performed.
After `412 leader moved`, a call with the same `step_key` from a new leader goes through the procedure of the batch door anew.
The subsystem translates the progress into the stream; the order of steps in the stream beyond the feed is not promised, the truth is `GET`.

Renewal of the turn does not change the generation, so parallel steps and renewals do not contend: the step call goes without a write of the leader, and the contract forbids renewal only in parallel with a target write.
A poisonous step does not hold the roots until `OPS_RUN_MAX`: after `OPS_STEP_TRIES` the operation goes on.
Failures in a row are counted in the leader's memory: a new turn holder counts anew; this gives\nup to `OPS_STEP_TRIES` more calls with the same key, but not an extra step.
At the disabling of the author the remaining steps of the operation get `cancel` (the round).
`cancel` also cancels waiting on pause.
A human pause is not removed by rebinding: `expired` is removed, `paused` remains — the operation waits.
The rebinding write is with `cas`.
A rebinding writes the journal `operation.rebound {id, was: <former jti>, now: <new jti>}`.
A conflict of the rebinding write at a read does not refuse\nthe answer: the rebinding repeats with the next request.
The progress stream of the subsystem rebinds likewise: it is a request of the author by a ticket.
While the author's tab is open, the operation goes. Closed — it goes until the deadline of the last token and waits for the author.
At a retry, a matching memory CAS of the acceptance batch permits 202.
At a retry, an unknown acceptance outcome retains the existing pending/cleanup rules.
Inside the new operation of a retry the chain of N1.4 acts as usual: a successful step over the root gives the version to the next one.
